test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 12 Oct 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What is the difference (in Rs.) between the compound interest, when interest is compounded 6-monthly, and the simple interest on a sum of Rs.10,000 for 1(1)/(2) years at 10% p.a.?
solution:
**Given:**

Principal = Rs. 10,000

Time = 1(1)/(2) = 3/2 years

Rate = 10%

**Formula used:**

A = P(1 + R/100)T

CI = (A – P)

SI = (P × R × T)/100

**Calculation:**

According to the question

CI for 6-monthly

P = Rs. 10,000

R = 10/2 = 5%

T = 1.5 years = 3 quarter

⇒ A = 10,000(1 + 5/100)³

⇒ 10,000(105/100)³

⇒ (10,000 × 21/20 × 21/20 × 21/20)

⇒ Rs. (92,610/8)

⇒ Rs. 11,576.25

CI = A – P

⇒ Rs. (11,576.25 – 10,000)

⇒ Rs. 1,576.25

Now,

SI = (10,000 × 10 × 3)/(2 × 100)

⇒ (10,000 × 30)/200

⇒ Rs. 1,500

Now,

Difference between CI and SI = Rs. (1,576.25 – 1,500)

⇒ Rs. 76.25

**∴ The required difference is Rs. 76.25**
